Package edu.ntnu.stud.idatg2003.backend.transformations

Class JuliaTransform

java.lang.Object
edu.ntnu.stud.idatg2003.backend.transformations.JuliaTransform
All Implemented Interfaces:
Transform2D
public class JuliaTransform extends Object implements Transform2D
The JuliaTransform class represents a complex transformation of the form z -> ±(z - c)^(1/n), where z is a complex number, and c is a complex constant. This transformation is used in generating Julia sets, a type of fractal.
Since:
0.0.0 (The version of Chaos-Game application when introduced)

    • transform

      public Vector2D transform(Vector2D z)
      Transforms a given complex number z according to the transformation 'z -> ±(z - c)^(1/n)'.

      This method calculates the nth root of the difference between the input complex number and the complex constant 'c'. The sign of the root is determined by the sign field of this JuliaTransform object. The transformation is given by: 

       z' = ±(z - c)^(1/n)
      where:
      • z is the input complex number
      • c is the complex constant
      • ± indicates that the sign can be either positive or negative

      Specified by:
      transform in interface Transform2D
      Parameters:
      z - The complex number to transform.
      Returns:
      The transformed complex number.
      Since:
      0.0.0

    • calculateJuliaSetPoint

      public int calculateJuliaSetPoint(double zx, double zy, int order, double cRe, double cIm, int maxIterations)
      Calculates the number of iterations for a given point in the Julia set.

      This method calculates how many iterations a complex number goes through before escaping a predefined radius (escape radius). The iteration process involves applying the transformation defined by the Julia set formula repeatedly until the magnitude of the resulting complex number exceeds the escape radius or the maximum number of iterations is reached.

      The transformation applied is: 

       Z(n+1) = (Z(n) - c)^(1/order) + c
      where:
      • Z is the complex number (zx, zy)
      • c is the constant complex number (cRe, cIm)
      • order is the order of the transformation

      Parameters:
      zx - The real part of the complex number.
      zy - The imaginary part of the complex number.
      order - The order of the transformation.
      cRe - The real part of the constant complex number.
      cIm - The imaginary part of the constant complex number.
      Returns:
      The number of iterations before the point escapes the Julia set boundary.
      Since:
      0.0.4

    • calculateMandelbrotSetPoint

      public int calculateMandelbrotSetPoint(double cx, double cy, int order, int maxIterations)
      Calculates the number of iterations for a given point in the Mandelbrot set.

      This method calculates how many iterations a complex number goes through before escaping a predefined radius (escape radius). The iteration process involves applying the transformation defined by the Mandelbrot set formula repeatedly until the magnitude of the resulting complex number exceeds the escape radius or the maximum number of iterations is reached.

      The transformation applied is: 

       Z(n+1) = Z(n)^order + c
      where:
      • Z is the complex number (initially (0, 0))
      • c is the constant complex number (cx, cy)
      • order is the order of the transformation

      Parameters:
      cx - The real part of the constant complex number.
      cy - The imaginary part of the constant complex number.
      order - The order of the transformation.
      maxIterations - The maximum number of iterations to perform.
      Returns:
      The number of iterations before the point escapes the Mandelbrot set boundary.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If the order or maxIterations is not positive.
      Since:
      0.0.3

    • iterate

      public Complex iterate(Complex z, Complex c, int order)
      Performs one iteration of the transformation for both Julia and Mandelbrot sets.

      This method calculates the next value of the complex number z in the iteration process by applying the transformation formula based on the specified order.

      The transformation for order 2 is: 

       Z(n+1) = Z(n)^2 + c
      The general transformation for higher orders is: 
       Z(n+1) = Z(n)^order + c
      where:
      • Z is the complex number being iterated
      • c is the constant complex number
      • order is the order of the transformation

      Parameters:
      z - The current complex number in the iteration process.
      c - The constant complex number.
      order - The order of the transformation.
      Returns:
      The next complex number after applying the transformation.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If the complex number z or c is null, or if the order is not positive.
      Since:
      0.0.3
